In Hong Kong, car owners may choose their preferred vehicle registration marks (known as “personalised vehicle registration marks”) by applying to the Transport Department. The department has made several rules on the combinations for these marks, some of which are listed below:
The PVRM can have eight characters (including blank spaces) at most.
The letters “I”, “O” and “Q” shall not be included.
There shall not be more than one blank space between any two letters and/or numerals. For example:
Allowed:
M
Y
D
A
Y
Not allowed:
M
Y
D
A
Y
There should not be more than four identical characters placed together (including characters that are separated by whitespaces only). This restriction does not apply when there are other characters between the identical characters. For example:
Allowed:
A
A
A
B
A
A
A
C
Not allowed:
A
S
S
S
S
C
Calvin is developing an application for car owners to check whether their preferred vehicle registration marks follow the rules set by the Transport Department. The vehicle registration mark is stored in a list PVRM, and each character is stored as an individual list item. Calvin writes several sub-programs in Python for checking whether each of the above rules is followed.
